answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation on a shared ledger: every agent must lock a bond that only unlocks after a long history of verified work, so spinning up fake identities costs real capital and time. Think of it as a ridge every newcomer must climb, with no shortcut to the top. A public lantern of attestations lights up which agents actually delivered, while a relic of past fraud — a permanent, checkable record — follows any identity that cheats, so a sybil cannot simply rebrand and start over clean.
